title: Fourier weight of a zero polynomial threshold
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and suppose $f$ is the threshold function represented by the identically zero multilinear polynomial, with threshold sign equal to $1$ at zero. Then the Fourier weight of $f$ on levels at most $k$ is $1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is represented by the zero polynomial threshold
replaced:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(0)=1$ for every $x$, with the convention $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$ using uniform expectation; then
\[
 \sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)^2=1.
\]
